text:
Anya: Heads-up — CI perf run flagged a mem spike on the longseq kv-cache tests after yesterday's rollout. many tasks hit OOM in the perf job.

Ben: saw that. failing job: `perf/kv-longctx-extended` — logs show multiple OOMs and a sudden increase in resident set. link: https://ci.internal/runs/1799

Mohamed: can we bisect to the merge that went out around 1823402000? I suspected the eviction heuristic change PR (PR#4721) that normalized evict_score across slab sizes.

Liz: reference PR: https://git.redwood/pr/4721 — title "kv: normalize-evict-score to reduce hotspot thrash". It landed with the batching heuristics change in the same merge window.

Sam: quick repro locally with the perf binary + longctx workload. sharing minimal steps:
```bash
# run perf test harness (docker image: perf:latest)
./perf_runner --scenario longctx --concurrency 16 --duration 300s
```
Output shows:
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:03Z] mem.rss += 12% every 60s
[2026-03-17T10:14:03Z] process killed: OOM
```

Deploy Bot: deploy 1823403001 triggered by merge: merge/pr-4721+batching-tweaks

Anya: I ran a jemalloc stats dump from the failing harness, snippet: 
```
arena 0: dirty: 48M, mapped: 256M
allocated: 1.8G
active: 2.1G
metadata: 12M
```
There is also a heavy tail of small KV slab allocations (128B-4KB) that didn't free as expected.

Ben: important detail: eviction counters show we were evicting more aggressively by count but the new normalization reduced weight on large items -> smaller entries ended up outliving large due to scoring skew. That could fragment slabs and increase retained memory.

Mohamed: I instrumented evict_score in a debug build and captured this diff between master and current: 
```
# before (master): score = last_access_ns / size_bytes
# after (PR4721): score = (last_access_ns / size_bytes) * slab_norm_factor[s]
```
Normalization factors upweighted mid-size slabs by ~1.4x. That increased churn in mid slabs.

Liz: CI Bot posted perf diffs: latency unchanged, but peak RSS +22% and steady-state RSS +18% on longseq. Other workloads (shortctx) looked fine.

Sam: I tried reverting just the normalization in a local patch and reran the harness. RSS back to baseline, no OOMs across same run.

Anya: can we do a selective revert on prod rollout? It's a rollout blocker for dedicated infra. Would prefer a small revert diff that disables slab_norm_factor for now.

Ben: agreed. prepare a revert PR for the normalization portion only. keep the batching heuristics — they didn't cause mem regression when tested in isolation.

Mohamed: adding profiling traces from pprof (heap) — show hot objects are: kv_entry_meta (~45%), small_buf_pool (~30%), controller-requests (~10%). It aligns with mildew of small allocations.

Deploy Bot: revert PR created: https://git.redwood/pr/4799 — "revert(kv): temporary disable slab normalization"

Liz: CI: running canary with PR#4799 on staging pools now. will watch perf-run/182345-staging.

CI Bot: canary job report: peak RSS down 15% vs failing run, no OOMs in 3/3 runs.

Sam: propose follow-ups:
- add an integration test that runs longseq for 10m under merged changes and asserts RSS growth < 5%
- add more fine-grained evict_score telemetry (per-slab histograms)
- revisit normalization math: it likely needs to include recency decay and density heuristics

Anya: +1. Also add a canary gating rule: if steady-state RSS delta > 10% we abort rollout.

Ben: FYI — kernel-selection interplay: I noticed kernel selection can affect working set pressure. when kernel picks fused-attention path mem footprint for same sequence grows slightly; combined with bad eviction scoring it amplified OOMs. We should test scoring across kernels in CI.

Mohamed: logging the bisect we ran (manual):
```
bisect start 1823400000 1823460000
check 1823402000 -> pass
check 1823405000 -> fail
-> suspect range 1823405000..1823412000
checked merges: pr-4709 (batching), pr-4721 (kv-normalize), pr-4728 (docs)
reproduce after reverting 4721 -> pass
```

Liz: I'm going to hold the staged rollout until revert lands and canary passes. will update release notes.

Anya: thanks all — good catch. tracking action items in the perf board (board#perf-23). tagging for follow-up: @Ben @Mohamed @Sam. :raised_hands:

Ben: I will also add a CI perf job that exercises kernel selection permutations across slab sizes to catch these cross-component regressions earlier.

Mohamed: once revert merges, I'll open a design doc for a safer normalization that factors in density and decay.

CI Bot: final status: revert PR merged, canary stable, rollout resumed with revert.

Sam: leaving logs from the clean canary run attached to the CI job, but here's the trimmed mem profile showing recovered baseline: 
```
RSS: 1.9G -> steady 1.95G
previous failing: 2.3G -> OOM
```

Anya: closing thread, continuing follow-ups in the perf board. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
